questions.stem: A car of mass $1500$ kg accelerates uniformly from rest to $20\text{ m/s}$ in $8.0$ s. Calculate the resultant force on the car.
questions.modelAnswer: First find the acceleration: $a = \dfrac{\Delta v}{t} = \dfrac{20 - 0}{8.0} = 2.5\text{ m/s}^2$. Then Newton's second law gives $F = ma = 1500 \times 2.5 = 3750\text{ N}$.

questions.stem: A trolley of mass $3.0$ kg moving at $4.0\text{ m/s}$ collides with a stationary trolley of mass $1.0$ kg. The trolleys stick together after the collision. Use conservation of momentum to calculate their common velocity after the collision.
markscheme: M1: momentum before $= mv = 3.0 \times 4.0 = 12\text{ kg m/s}$
questions.modelAnswer: Total momentum is conserved. Before the collision only the moving trolley carries momentum: $p = 3.0 \times 4.0 = 12\text{ kg m/s}$. After the collision the combined mass is $4.0$ kg, so $12 = 4.0v$, giving $v = 3.0\text{ m/s}$ in the original direction of motion.

questions.stem: A uniform beam is balanced on a pivot. A force of $200\text{ N}$ acts $0.30\text{ m}$ to the left of the pivot. What force, applied $0.50\text{ m}$ to the right of the pivot, keeps the beam in equilibrium?
markscheme: M1: moment $= F \times$ perpendicular distance $= 200 \times 0.30 = 60\text{ N m}$
M1: applies the principle of moments (clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment, $0.50F = 60$)
questions.modelAnswer: For equilibrium the total anticlockwise moment equals the total clockwise moment about the pivot. The $200\text{ N}$ force gives a moment of $200 \times 0.30 = 60\text{ N m}$. So the balancing force satisfies $0.50F = 60$, hence $F = 120\text{ N}$.

questions.stem: A transformer has $1150$ turns on its primary coil and $50$ turns on its secondary coil. The primary is connected to a $230\text{ V}$ a.c. supply. Calculate the secondary p.d., assuming $100\%$ efficiency.
questions.modelAnswer: For an ideal transformer $\dfrac{V_p}{V_s} = \dfrac{N_p}{N_s}$, so $V_s = V_p \times \dfrac{N_s}{N_p} = 230 \times \dfrac{50}{1150} = 10\text{ V}$. This is a step-down transformer.

questions.stem: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of $6$ hours. A sample has a corrected count rate of $800$ counts/min. What is the corrected count rate after $18$ hours?
questions.modelAnswer: The count rate halves every $6$ hours. $18$ hours is three half-lives, so $800 \to 400 \to 200 \to 100$. After $18$ hours the corrected count rate is $100$ counts/min.

questions.stem: The Moon orbits the Earth in an approximately circular orbit of radius $3.84 \times 10^{8}\text{ m}$ with a period of $27.3$ days. Calculate the Moon's orbital speed. ($1$ day $= 8.64 \times 10^{4}$ s.)
markscheme: M1: converts the period to seconds ($27.3 \times 8.64 \times 10^{4} = 2.36 \times 10^{6}$ s)
questions.modelAnswer: For circular motion $v = \dfrac{2\pi r}{T}$. Convert the period: $T = 27.3 \times 8.64 \times 10^{4} = 2.36 \times 10^{6}$ s. Then $v = \dfrac{2\pi \times 3.84 \times 10^{8}}{2.36 \times 10^{6}} = \dfrac{2.41 \times 10^{9}}{2.36 \times 10^{6}} \approx 1.02 \times 10^{3}\text{ m/s}$, about $1$ km/s.

questions.stem: A ball of mass $0.050$ kg travelling at $12\text{ m/s}$ hits a wall and rebounds at $8\text{ m/s}$ in the opposite direction. The impact lasts $0.020$ s. Calculate the average force exerted on the ball by the wall.
markscheme: M1: $\Delta p = m\Delta v = 0.050 \times (12 - (-8)) = 1.0\text{ kg m/s}$ (rebound sign change handled)
questions.modelAnswer: Taking the initial direction as positive, the velocity changes from $+12$ to $-8\text{ m/s}$, so $\Delta v = 20\text{ m/s}$ and $\Delta p = 0.050 \times 20 = 1.0\text{ kg m/s}$. The average force is $F = \dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{1.0}{0.020} = 50\text{ N}$.

questions.stem: A radium nucleus decays by alpha emission: $^{226}_{88}\text{Ra} \rightarrow {}^{a}_{b}\text{Rn} + {}^{4}_{2}\text{He}$. Determine the values of $a$ and $b$.
questions.modelAnswer: In any nuclear equation both nucleon number and proton number are conserved. The alpha particle carries away $4$ nucleons and $2$ protons, so $a = 226 - 4 = 222$ and $b = 88 - 2 = 86$. The daughter nucleus is $^{222}_{86}\text{Rn}$.
